// The certify1 differential corpus (RB9-F5-5): mutations of the documents of the certify1 suite (validator pkg/proof/v2/testdata/certify1, the anchored
// certify form: evidence 2.1 links, the genesis link, the accounting of the set check, the window of an update), each applied to the base document's
// JSON tree and judged by proofv2.VerifyPortable. A verdict is one of: verified (with the report summary), named (a NamedState with its partition and
// block), certify (a *CertifyState with its code and fields, RB9-F5 section 3) or plain (any other refusal; its wording is not compared).
//
//	GOWORK=off go run ./cmd/xtsgen -fixtures <certen-sdk>/packages/verify/test/fixtures/s3-f5 -out <certen-sdk>/packages/verify/test/fixtures/s3-f5-go -per 30 certify1
//
// A mutation on which Go panics or answers differently on repeated runs is not recorded (counted in skipped and printed to stderr).
package main

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"math/rand"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime/debug"
	"strings"

	proofv2 "github.com/certen/independant-validator/pkg/proof/v2"
)

// CExpect is what the validator's verifier answers for a certify1 document.
type CExpect struct {
	V       string    `json:"v"` // verified | named | certify | plain
	State   *StateOut `json:"state,omitempty"`
	Code    string    `json:"code,omitempty"`
	Fields  []string  `json:"fields,omitempty"`
	Msg     string    `json:"msg,omitempty"`
	Summary *Summary  `json:"summary,omitempty"`
}

type CMutation struct {
	ID      string  `json:"id"`
	Base    int     `json:"base"`
	Op      string  `json:"op"`
	Patches []Patch `json:"patches"`
	Expect  CExpect `json:"expect"`
}

type CFile struct {
	Format      string `json:"format"`
	Description string `json:"description"`
	Validator   string `json:"validator"`
	// ManifestSha256 is the hash of the certify1 manifest.json the corpus was written over: a corpus is stale when the suite is re-synced.
	ManifestSha256 string      `json:"manifestSha256"`
	Bases          []string    `json:"bases"`
	BaseSha256     []string    `json:"baseSha256"`
	BaseExpect     []CExpect   `json:"baseExpect"`
	Mutations      []CMutation `json:"mutations"`
	Skipped        struct {
		Panics int `json:"panics"`
		Flaky  int `json:"flaky"`
	} `json:"skipped"`
}

func judgeC(doc []byte) (e CExpect, ok bool) {
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			ok = false
			lastPanic = fmt.Sprintf("%v | %s", r, topFrames(debug.Stack(), 6))
		}
	}()
	p := new(proofv2.Portable)
	if err := json.Unmarshal(doc, p); err != nil {
		return CExpect{V: "plain", Msg: err.Error()}, true
	}
	rep, err := proofv2.VerifyPortable(p)
	if err == nil {
		return CExpect{V: "verified", Summary: summarize(rep)}, true
	}
	var cs *proofv2.CertifyState
	if errors.As(err, &cs) {
		return CExpect{V: "certify", Code: cs.Code, Fields: append([]string{}, cs.Fields...), Msg: err.Error()}, true
	}
	var ns *proofv2.NamedState
	if errors.As(err, &ns) {
		return CExpect{V: "named", State: &StateOut{ns.Code, ns.Partition, ns.Block}, Msg: err.Error()}, true
	}
	return CExpect{V: "plain", Msg: err.Error()}, true
}

func sameC(a, b CExpect) bool {
	if a.V != b.V {
		return false
	}
	switch a.V {
	case "plain":
		return true // the wording may differ between runs by map order; the class is what is stable
	}
	ja, _ := json.Marshal(a)
	jb, _ := json.Marshal(b)
	return string(ja) == string(jb)
}

func judgeCStable(doc []byte, f *CFile) (CExpect, bool) {
	runs := 4
	if len(doc) > 100_000 {
		runs = 2
	}
	a, ok := judgeC(doc)
	if !ok {
		f.Skipped.Panics++
		return a, false
	}
	for i := 1; i < runs; i++ {
		b, ok := judgeC(doc)
		if !ok {
			f.Skipped.Panics++
			return a, false
		}
		if !sameC(a, b) {
			f.Skipped.Flaky++
			lastFlaky = a.V + " vs " + b.V
			return a, false
		}
	}
	return a, true
}

// receiptLike reports whether a node is a merkle receipt as the document spells it.
func receiptLike(v any) bool {
	m, ok := v.(map[string]any)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	_, hasStart := m["start"]
	_, hasAnchor := m["anchor"]
	_, hasEntries := m["entries"]
	return hasStart && hasAnchor && hasEntries
}

var epilogues = []string{"05010a", "07010a", "08020102", "0a00", "1f01aa", "2001aa", "2101aa", "00", "80", "0101", "0601", "06020a0b", "ff", "", "0701", "09"}

// targeted returns the structural mutations of the certify form for a base document: every one a change a certify1 verifier must judge as Go does.
func targeted(r *rand.Rand, doc map[string]any) ([]Patch, string) {
	ev, _ := doc["evidence"].(map[string]any)
	var nodes []node
	collect(ev, []any{"evidence"}, &nodes)
	var receipts, records []node
	// An unknown trailing field is aimed where the certify form reads it: the receipts of the links and of the genesis link (a link that does not
	// decode is certify_link_invalid) and the minor-root records of certify and of the set check's hops (a record tolerates a trailing field 5..32
	// and refuses one it cannot place). Every other receipt of a document is decoded by the verifier's older code, which is not under test here.
	for _, n := range nodes {
		if len(n.path) >= 2 && (n.path[1] == "links" || n.path[1] == "genesisLink") && receiptLike(n.v) && len(n.path) <= 3 {
			receipts = append(receipts, n)
		}
		isRun := (len(n.path) == 3 && n.path[1] == "certify") || (len(n.path) == 4 && n.path[1] == "check" && n.path[2] == "hops")
		if m, ok := n.v.(map[string]any); ok && isRun {
			if _, has := m["signatures"]; has {
				if _, has2 := m["anchor"]; has2 {
					records = append(records, n)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	pick := func(l []node) (node, bool) {
		if len(l) == 0 {
			return node{}, false
		}
		return l[r.Intn(len(l))], true
	}
	links, _ := ev["links"].([]any)
	certify, _ := ev["certify"].([]any)
	switch r.Intn(14) {
	case 0:
		if n, ok := pick(receipts); ok {
			return []Patch{{Path: append(append([]any(nil), n.path...), "$epilogue"), Op: "set", Value: epilogues[r.Intn(len(epilogues))], HasV: true}}, "epilogue-receipt@" + pathString(n.path)
		}
	case 1:
		if n, ok := pick(records); ok {
			return []Patch{{Path: append(append([]any(nil), n.path...), "$epilogue"), Op: "set", Value: epilogues[r.Intn(len(epilogues))], HasV: true}}, "epilogue-record@" + pathString(n.path)
		}
	case 2:
		return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "version"}, Op: "set", Value: "2.0", HasV: true}}, "version20"
	case 3:
		if len(certify) > 0 {
			i := r.Intn(len(certify))
			if m, ok := certify[i].(map[string]any); ok {
				if _, has := m["rootProof"]; has {
					return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "certify", i, "rootProof"}, Op: "delete"}}, fmt.Sprintf("rootproof-drop@%d", i)
				}
			}
		}
	case 4:
		if len(links) > 0 {
			i := r.Intn(len(links))
			return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "links"}, Op: "dropIndex", I: i}}, fmt.Sprintf("link-drop@%d", i)
		}
	case 5:
		if len(links) > 0 {
			i := r.Intn(len(links))
			return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "links"}, Op: "dup", I: i}}, fmt.Sprintf("link-dup@%d", i)
		}
	case 6:
		if len(links) >= 2 {
			return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "links"}, Op: "swap", I: 0, J: len(links) - 1}}, "link-swap"
		}
	case 7:
		return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "genesisLink"}, Op: "delete"}}, "genesis-link-drop"
	case 8:
		return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "genesisLink"}, Op: "set", Value: nil, HasV: true}}, "genesis-link-null"
	case 9:
		return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "links"}, Op: "set", Value: nil, HasV: true}}, "links-null"
	case 10:
		if len(links) > 0 {
			i := r.Intn(len(links))
			return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "links", i}, Op: "set", Value: nil, HasV: true}}, fmt.Sprintf("link-null@%d", i)
		}
	case 11:
		if len(links) > 0 {
			i := r.Intn(len(links))
			return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "links", i, "entries"}, Op: "set", Value: []any{}, HasV: true}}, fmt.Sprintf("link-entries-empty@%d", i)
		}
	case 12:
		if len(certify) > 0 {
			i := r.Intn(len(certify))
			return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "certify"}, Op: "dropIndex", I: i}}, fmt.Sprintf("certify-drop@%d", i)
		}
	case 13:
		if len(certify) >= 2 {
			return []Patch{{Path: []any{"evidence", "certify"}, Op: "swap", I: 0, J: len(certify) - 1}}, "certify-swap"
		}
	}
	return nil, ""
}

func certify1Mutations(fixtures, out string, per int) error {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(fixtures, "certify1", "manifest.json"))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	msum := sha256.Sum256(raw)
	var m struct {
		Cases []struct {
			File string `json:"file"`
		} `json:"cases"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	f := &CFile{Format: "certen:certify1-mutations:v1",
		Description: "Mutations of the certify1 vectors (RB9-F5 anchored certify form), each applied to the base document's JSON tree and judged by proofv2.VerifyPortable: the verdict is verified (summary), named (state, partition, block), certify (code, fields) or plain (class only). A mutation on which Go panics or answers differently on two runs is not recorded."}
	f.ManifestSha256 = hex.EncodeToString(msum[:])
	// The suite's documents, then the evidence 2.0 documents of the earlier corpora (relative to the fixtures directory, XTS_EXTRA_BASES, comma-separated;
	// a .gz is read decompressed and hashed as stored): the sweeps reach the 2.0 form's receipts too.
	var bpaths []string
	for _, c := range m.Cases {
		bpaths = append(bpaths, "certify1/"+c.File)
	}
	if extra := os.Getenv("XTS_EXTRA_BASES"); extra != "" {
		bpaths = append(bpaths, strings.Split(extra, ",")...)
	}
	for bi, bpath := range bpaths {
		f.Bases = append(f.Bases, bpath)
		stored, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(fixtures, bpath))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		rawDoc, err := readDoc(filepath.Join(fixtures, bpath))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		sum := sha256.Sum256(stored)
		f.BaseSha256 = append(f.BaseSha256, hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]))
		var base any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(rawDoc, &base); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", bpath, err)
		}
		canon, _ := json.Marshal(base)
		be, ok := judgeCStable(canon, f)
		if !ok {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: Go is unstable on the base document", bpath)
		}
		f.BaseExpect = append(f.BaseExpect, be)

		var nodes []node
		collect(base.(map[string]any)["evidence"], []any{"evidence"}, &nodes)
		doc := base.(map[string]any)
		for _, k := range []string{"pin", "format"} {
			nodes = append(nodes, node{[]any{k}, doc[k]})
		}
		if g, ok := doc["genesis"].(map[string]any); ok {
			for _, k := range []string{"rootChainAnchor", "stateTreeAnchor", "networkRecord", "globalsRecord"} {
				nodes = append(nodes, node{[]any{"genesis", k}, g[k]})
			}
		}
		for k := 0; k < per; k++ {
			r := rand.New(rand.NewSource(seedOf(bpath, fmt.Sprint(k))))
			var ps []Patch
			var ops []string
			if k%3 == 0 { // a third of the mutations are the certify form's own structural changes
				p, name := targeted(r, doc)
				if p == nil {
					continue
				}
				ps, ops = p, []string{name}
			} else {
				count := 1
				if r.Intn(4) == 0 {
					count = 2
				}
				for cc := 0; cc < count; cc++ {
					t := nodes[r.Intn(len(nodes))]
					for tries := 0; tries < 4; tries++ {
						switch t.v.(type) {
						case map[string]any, []any:
							if r.Intn(3) != 0 {
								t = nodes[r.Intn(len(nodes))]
								continue
							}
						}
						break
					}
					p, name := mutate(r, t, "")
					ps = append(ps, p)
					ops = append(ops, name+"@"+pathString(p.Path))
				}
			}
			mutated, ok := applyPatches(base, ps)
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			docBytes, err := json.Marshal(mutated)
			if err != nil {
				continue
			}
			lastPanic = ""
			e, ok := judgeCStable(docBytes, f)
			if !ok {
				if lastPanic != "" {
					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "PANIC %s#%02d [%s]: %s\n", bpath, k, strings.Join(ops, " + "), lastPanic)
				} else {
					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "FLAKY %s#%02d [%s]: %s\n", bpath, k, strings.Join(ops, " + "), lastFlaky)
				}
				continue
			}
			f.Mutations = append(f.Mutations, CMutation{ID: fmt.Sprintf("%s#%02d", bpath, k), Base: bi, Op: strings.Join(ops, " + "), Patches: ps, Expect: e})
		}
		sweepCertify1(base, bi, bpath, f)
	}
	return writeJSON(filepath.Join(out, "certify1-mutations.json.gz"), f)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the sweeps (TS parity round B6 after F5-5): every receipt member of every base document is given each unplaceable and placeable trailing field,
// and every number of every base document is set to the edge values of a uint64. They are exhaustive per path class (a path with every array index
// replaced by *), not drawn at random, so a verifier that reads one receipt or one number differently from Go is found by construction.

// classOf spells a path with every array index as *.
func classOf(p []any) string {
	parts := make([]string, len(p))
	for i, e := range p {
		if _, ok := e.(int); ok {
			parts[i] = "*"
		} else {
			parts[i] = fmt.Sprint(e)
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, "/")
}

// sweepEpilogues are the trailing fields (merkle.Receipt, ReceiptEntry and api.MinorRootRecord keep what follows their last known field as extra data;
// the reader refuses a field number it cannot place after what it has read, or above 32): EVERY field number 0-8 and 31-33 and 64 with a value, the bare
// bytes that open such a field (01 03 04 21 ff 80 8001), field 4 as a record's root proof (0400, 04020100), a field 6 that reads as one more entry
// (0601, 06020a0b), 05010a (an unplaceable field 5 after the entries) and 07010a (an unknown field 7 kept as extra data).
var sweepEpilogues = func() []string {
	var out []string
	for _, n := range []int{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 31, 32, 33, 64} {
		out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%02x01aa", n))
	}
	return append(out, "01", "03", "04", "21", "ff", "80", "8001", "0400", "04020100", "0601", "06020a0b", "05010a", "07010a")
}()

// sweepBases is the number of documents a path class is swept in (see sweepCertify1).
const sweepBases = 3

var sweepUse = map[string]int{}

var u64Values = []string{"9007199254740991", "9007199254740992", "9223372036854775808", "18446744073709551615", "18446744073709551616"}

func isReceiptNode(n node) bool {
	m, ok := n.v.(map[string]any)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	if receiptLike(m) {
		return true
	}
	if len(n.path) > 0 {
		switch n.path[len(n.path)-1] {
		case "receipt", "continuedReceipt", "genesisLink", "stateReceipt":
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func isEntryNode(n node) bool {
	m, ok := n.v.(map[string]any)
	if !ok || len(n.path) < 2 {
		return false
	}
	_, hasHash := m["hash"]
	_, hasRight := m["right"]
	_, isInList := n.path[len(n.path)-1].(int)
	return hasHash && hasRight && isInList && n.path[len(n.path)-2] == "entries"
}

func isRecordNode(n node) bool {
	m, ok := n.v.(map[string]any)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	_, a := m["signatures"]
	_, b := m["anchor"]
	return a && b
}

func sweepCertify1(base any, bi int, bpath string, f *CFile) {
	doc := base.(map[string]any)
	var nodes []node
	collect(doc, nil, &nodes)
	seq := 0
	record := func(ops string, ps []Patch) {
		mutated, ok := applyPatches(base, ps)
		if !ok {
			return
		}
		docBytes, err := json.Marshal(mutated)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		lastPanic = ""
		e, ok := judgeCStable(docBytes, f)
		id := fmt.Sprintf("%s#sweep%03d", bpath, seq)
		seq++
		if !ok {
			if lastPanic != "" {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "PANIC %s [%s]: %s\n", id, ops, lastPanic)
			} else {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "FLAKY %s [%s]: %s\n", id, ops, lastFlaky)
			}
			return
		}
		f.Mutations = append(f.Mutations, CMutation{ID: id, Base: bi, Op: ops, Patches: ps, Expect: e})
	}
	form := "2.1"
	if ev, ok := doc["evidence"].(map[string]any); ok {
		if v, ok := ev["version"].(string); ok {
			form = v
		}
	}
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	once := func(kind string, n node) bool {
		k := kind + "|" + classOf(n.path)
		if seen[k] {
			return false
		}
		seen[k] = true
		k = form + "|" + k // a class is swept in the first sweepBases documents of each form (2.1 and 2.0)
		// A class is swept in the first sweepBases documents that hold it, so a corpus over 46 documents does not repeat the same member 46 times; the
		// anchor's own block and root chain index are swept in every document, as what follows them (a link, a window, a replay) differs by document.
		last, _ := n.path[len(n.path)-1].(string)
		if last != "minorBlockIndex" && last != "rootChainIndex" {
			sweepUse[k]++
			if sweepUse[k] > sweepBases {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	}
	for _, n := range nodes {
		if isReceiptNode(n) || isEntryNode(n) || isRecordNode(n) {
			kind := "receipt"
			if isEntryNode(n) {
				kind = "entry"
			}
			if isRecordNode(n) {
				kind = "record"
			}
			if once("epi-"+kind, n) {
				for _, e := range sweepEpilogues {
					record("sweep-epilogue-"+e+"@"+pathString(n.path), []Patch{{Path: append(append([]any(nil), n.path...), "$epilogue"), Op: "set", Value: e, HasV: true}})
				}
			}
		}
		if _, isNum := n.v.(float64); isNum && len(n.path) > 0 && once("u64", n) {
			for _, v := range u64Values {
				record("sweep-u64-"+v+"@"+pathString(n.path), []Patch{{Path: n.path, Op: "setNumber", To: v}})
			}
		}
		// a member a document may lack: an absent or null message or receipt is judged at the import (finding RB9-F5-5-F3)
		if len(n.path) > 0 {
			if last, ok := n.path[len(n.path)-1].(string); ok && (last == "message" || last == "receipt") && once("drop", n) {
				record("sweep-delete@"+pathString(n.path), []Patch{{Path: n.path, Op: "delete"}})
				record("sweep-null@"+pathString(n.path), []Patch{{Path: n.path, Op: "set", Value: nil, HasV: true}})
			}
		}
	}
}
